your_life.name: Inspector Arun Mehra
your_life.recollections:
Before the district office, before the uniform, there was Mill Lane: the rasp of your father's wheel plane through the open workshop door and Tara making you wait while she tied her shoes. You left Bhairav's Hollow with a habit of looking back at the chapel turn. Twelve winters have passed since Mercy House sent the letter saying your sister had died of fever. Requests for the original papers have filled a drawer in your room at headquarters; the paper has aged more visibly than the answers have changed.

Leena used to know where you kept that drawer. You lived together for three years, separated, and learned to write letters about the practical things that remained. Her mother once set tea in front of you after Tara's funeral. Raghav's signature is familiar from replies to your requests. You remember the weight of the cup and the silence around it.

Kabir has worked beside you for six years. You remember the floodwater in the cellar where you pulled him out, but also uneventful journeys, poor meals and the little habits by which colleagues become familiar. Dr. Mira Sen's invitation brought you back on leave: she wanted to discuss an old family record. No death had been reported when you set out. Now the coach journey is behind you, the town is under snow, and you have reached Mercy House.

place.name: Mercy House courtyard
place.description: Snow collects along the courtyard walls without yet settling in the wheel ruts. A gate lamp turns the falling flakes into brief bright scratches. Behind you Mercy House has too many dark windows; ahead, the road drops toward the square. A narrower way runs beside the wall to Dev's winter garden. A kitchen clang carries into the courtyard and is gone almost before you turn toward it.

people.name: Sera Dutt
people.appearance: The cook wipes hands that are already dry on the edge of her apron. Her eyes return to the nearest door when voices rise. She starts a sentence twice before choosing its first word.

people.name: Kabir Mehta
people.appearance: Your constable shifts his notebook into the hand he uses when expecting instructions. The gesture is familiar from years of work together.

people.name: Anya Paul
people.appearance: A young constable holds a pencil against a small notebook. She waits for a specific instruction and distinguishes what she has seen from what she has been told.

opening.assignment: Follow up with the person you previously spoke to about the service hatch. Obtain a first-hand account and establish the physical match between acquired garment pieces. Report the match with sources; an unidentified sleeve does not establish who delivered a fatal injury.

notes.label: body
notes.description: The woman has no detectable pulse. There is a recent injury at the temple and wet blood beneath her head.

notes.label: brass seal
notes.description: A heavy seal lies beside the desk. Dark wet staining marks one edge.

notes.label: torn cuff
notes.description: A small scrap of dark wool is caught under the desk edge. It is not a complete garment.

notes.label: bloodied sleeve
notes.description: A sleeve has been torn off and folded against the wound. Dark staining spreads through the inside fold.

notes.question: What can be seen through the hatch?
notes.words: I can describe what I remember. Please distinguish it from anything I only heard.

recollections.text: The service hatch shows only part of the archive.
I heard gossip that Dev threatened Mira, but did not hear Dev say it.

notes.label: signed shopping note
notes.description: A shopping note has been held flat by the sugar bowl. “Kamala—please collect flour and lamp oil tomorrow. Leave the account in the kitchen tin; I shall settle it after breakfast. S. Das.” The ordinary household hand has a distinctive overwritten lower-case d. A dry ring from the bowl crosses the bottom corner.

notes.label: household shawl
notes.description: A dark wool shawl has a freshly torn cuff and recent blood marks. A laundry tag bears S. Das.

notes.label: private letters
notes.description: Two letters are folded inside a plain wrapper. One addresses Leena in Mira’s hand: “I love you. That is the part of this I can write without revising it. Meet me at the chapel tomorrow, before the lamps are lit.” A reply signed Leena refers to their private meeting yesterday and asks that the letters be kept from household gossip.

notes.question: What did you personally see through the hatch?
notes.words: I can describe what I remember. Please distinguish it from anything I only heard.

recollections.text: The service hatch shows only part of the archive.
I heard gossip that Dev threatened Mira, but did not hear Dev say it.
I heard a woman demand a statement through the hatch.
Through the narrow hatch I saw a dark sleeve move, then heard a heavy blow. I could not see the face.
A heavy noise and cry came from the archive. I did not see what struck anyone.

args.narrative: Sera’s first-hand account is that she saw a dark sleeve move through the narrow service hatch, then heard a heavy blow; she could not see the face or what struck Mira (r9). The torn wool scrap from beneath the archive desk physically fits the missing cuff of the blood-marked, tagged household shawl: the torn edge, weave, and repair stitches continue across the join, with recent blood marks on the joined edge (r3, r7, r12). This establishes a garment match and links the garment to the struggle; it does not identify who wore it or establish who delivered the fatal injury.
